summary: Mars’ Hidden Secrets is an educational and entertaining comic designed for children aged 7–10. It introduces Spirit and Opportunity, two Mars rovers whose missions have ended but whose discoveries continue to contribute to our understanding of the planet. Through engaging illustrations and simple dialogue, the comic explains what these robotic explorers discovered during their missions, especially the clues they found about water on ancient Mars. By turning scientific discoveries into an accessible adventure, we aim to help children understand how space exploration benefits humanity. Learning about these achievements at an early age can support children’s personal development while encouraging curiosity, scientific thinking, and a sense of responsibility toward society. Our project takes a small step toward inspiring the next generation to ask questions, explore new ideas, and become individuals who can make meaningful contributions to humanity.
details: Our project, Mars’ Hidden Secrets, engages children’s visual perception and thinking skills to help them learn through an enjoyable comic about the discoveries made by space vehicles whose missions have ended. By introducing these discoveries and their value to humanity, we aim to provide both individual and social benefits. For each child, the comic offers a meaningful way to spend time while gaining useful knowledge. In the longer term, this learning may help children become individuals who contribute positively to their communities. The story also encourages readers to ask questions, consider different ideas, and develop a more curious and thoughtful perspective. We hope to nurture children’s interest in educational comics and inspire them to share what they learn with others. As one child tells another, this knowledge could spread, creating a positive ripple effect within their communities. To ensure scientific accuracy, we consulted resources published by NASA and used this information as the foundation for our own fictional story. We then developed an illustrated draft, added dialogue, and used artificial intelligence tools to turn our design into a digital comic. Working together as a team, we first checked the scientific information, exchanged ideas, and created a scenario that we believed would communicate the subject effectively to children aged 7–10. We initially visualized the story by hand, without software or artificial intelligence, and added dialogue to develop it into a comic. We did not use artificial intelligence during the initial brainstorming and story-development stages; we later used ChatGPT to help produce the digital version. Throughout the project, we considered environmental responsibility, accessibility, and cost so that as many children as possible could benefit. For printed copies, we aimed to use recyclable materials and keep production costs low. If the comic moves into larger-scale production, we would like to seek public support or government purchasing to make copies available to children from families with limited financial resources. The creative concept and initial story were developed from our own ideas, while NASA resources supported the scientific content and AI tools assisted with digital production. Our main goal is to help children gain accurate knowledge, develop their curiosity, and grow into individuals who can contribute to both their own lives and the wider community.
